**What is this feature?**

Title: Annotations: backfill time_end = time and add NOT NULL constraint

**What is this feature?**

Follow-up to https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132713, which stopped writing `NULL` `time_end` values for point annotations. This PR:

- Backfills existing point annotations with a `NULL` `time_end` to `time`, and adds a `NOT NULL` constraint so _all_ annotations have a `time_end`
- Replaces the points/ranges `UNION` in `List` with a single query ordered by `time_end DESC, time DESC, name`
- Replaces the existing list indexes with new ones matching the above ordering, replacing the namespace+dashboard+panel index with just a namespace+dashboard index as that is the primary query path from the UI.
- Makes `Get` deterministic with `ORDER BY time DESC`

**Why do we need this feature?**

The `UNION` made every List query plan each partition twice. This ends up being the bulk of List query latency when under load. With `time_end` always set, a single query can leverage the new indexes to more efficiently filter to the ordered data.

This also sets up https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/133408, which partitions on `time_end` so old partitions can be pruned entirely, which was the primary goal of a partitioned table in the first place.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:



Related to https://github.com/grafana/grafana-org/issues/1006

Title: Unified storage: let compiled-in apps outside apps/ register a manifest

Storage and search pods decide which label selectors they can answer from the search index. Until now that decision used the list of apps built into the Grafana binary. With this change they read the list from the app-platform API server instead, so a newly installed app is picked up without a Grafana release. The code side landed in grafana/grafana#133148 but has been inert, because the deployments were not configured for it.

Enabled in dev only, through `rollout-config/dev.jsonnet`. Later waves pick it up through the normal rollout copy.

Both storage-api and search-api are configured. Each points at the app-platform CA where its own pod mounts it: storage-api has it at `/etc/cloud-app-platform-ca/ca.crt` already (the tenant watcher uses it), search-api gets it projected into `/etc/kubernetes-secrets/cloud-app-platform-ca.crt`. The poll interval is left at the default of one hour. Token and token exchange URL were already configured for other clients, so nothing was added there.

Enabling this also grants the storage service identity read access to appmanifests, cluster-wide, on the shared access policy token.

One dev cell (`dev-us-central-0.unified-storage-dev-002`) already ran this on search pods, so its per-cell override is removed as redundant. That cell shows only the storage-api half of the diff. ops and prod cells render unchanged.

I could not run `tk diff` (no cluster access from here), so this was checked with before/after `tk show` on dev-us-east-0.unified-storage-dev-001, dev-us-central-0.unified-storage-dev-002 and ops-eu-south-0.unified-storage-ops-002.

Rollout restarts both storage-api and search-api pods in dev, through the config hash.

How we will know it worked:

- `search_manifest_watcher_polls_total{result="success"}` climbing and `result="error"` flat — errors here would mean the appmanifests grant is not effective
- `search_manifest_watcher_manifests` above the count of apps built into the binary
- `search_manifest_watcher_reloads_total` incrementing when an app manifest changes

`Replace` now warns when a swap removes a kind that currently has search fields. Losing them is otherwise silent — searches on those fields still succeed and match nothing, and the field-set hash lives in the index metadata, so recovery needs an index rebuild rather than a restart.

Rollout note: this PR on its own changes no hashes, since nothing in OSS registers a manifest. Once a distribution registers one, only the newly declared kind rebuilds its index — the field-set hash is stored and compared per kind, so kinds that already had search fields keep their hash, and kinds without search fields have no hash to compare and are untouched.

Title: SSOSettings: add read-only SSOSetting support to standalone apiserver

## What

The always-on `iam.grafana.app` apiserver (`NewAPIService`) never wired a store for the `SSOSetting` kind, so it did not serve the kind even with `kubernetesSsoSettingsApi` enabled (only the in-process `RegisterAPIService` path did). This adds a lean read-only ssosettings service, backed by the per-request legacy `sso_setting` table, and wires it into `NewAPIService`.

The standalone apiserver now serves the `SSOSetting` kind read-only under the same flag, so the frontend and edge-auth (MTEA) services can read a stack's SSO configuration through `iam.grafana.app` without depending on the in-process monolith.

## How

- New `ProvideReadOnlyDBService` reads and redacts secrets by field name (no decrypt, so it needs no secrets/config service); writes return an error.
- Reuses the existing `sso.NewLegacyStore` wrapper — no new `NewAPIService` parameters, no enterprise wiring change.
- No behavior change to the in-process (`RegisterAPIService`) path.

## Notes

- Reads only; secrets are always redacted.
- Authorization for these reads is handled separately (RBAC).
- Pairs with the dev-cell flag enablement in grafana/deployment_tools#728400.

Title: Alerting: Fix RouteGetReceivers UID resolution and move status retrieval into ReceiverService

## Context

`RouteGetReceivers` (`GET /api/alertmanager/grafana/config/api/v1/receivers`) returns receiver status (active state, per-integration health) sourced from the org's running Alertmanager, which only knows receivers by **Name**. To satisfy authorization, which is keyed by UID, the handler needed a UID for each AM-reported receiver. Since no receiver UID is persisted independently today, the handler got one the only way available: hashing the name (`legacy_storage.NameToUid`). This is consistent with how every other part of ngalert computes a receiver's UID right now, but only because nothing has decoupled UID from Name yet.

Once that lands, the name will not be sufficient to determine permissions and this handler does not have easy access to the real receivers as written. This PR removes that landmine by making `ReceiverService` the single source of truth for fetching AM-reported statuses.

- Fetching and filtering receiver status is now owned entirely by `ReceiverService`, via a new `amStatusFetcher` dependency (`MultiOrgAlertmanager.GetReceiverStatuses`.
- `ReceiverService.StatusMetadata` fetches AM status and maps the given receivers to their live AM status by Name.
- `ReceiverService.GetReceiverStatuses` is the permission-aware, org-wide wrapper on top of `StatusMetadata`. It handles fetching the stored receivers and filtering to only what the caller can read. 
- The reason the above two methods are split is to follow existing metadata function patterns, so that we might eventually move these statuses directly to the receiver API resource responses. If done, `GetReceiverStatuses` will no longer be necessary.
- `RouteGetReceivers` is now a thin call to `receiverService.GetReceiverStatuses`.

Note: This adds an extra DB hit to the API call (previously it only hit for the permissions check), but this is hard to get around without making our AM implementations UID-aware.

Part of grafana/alerting-squad#1730.
tasks.goldTitle: Alerting: Fix RouteGetReceivers UID resolution and move status retrieval into ReceiverService

Title: Explore: Add RudderStack events for the metrics sidebar

## Description


Adds the four RudderStack events Analytics signed off on for the Signal Explorer metrics sidebar, so the A/B test has behavioural data to read. The sidebar had no instrumentation at all before this; the feature stays behind the existing `grafana.exploreMetricsSidebar` toggle, so nothing is emitted with the flag off.

## Changes

* New `SignalExplorer/tracking.ts` holding typed wrappers for `signal_explorer_panel_opened`, `signal_explorer_metric_expanded`, `signal_explorer_search_performed` and `signal_explorer_metrics_metadata_viewed`, so the event names and property keys live in one place.
* `panel_opened` fires once per sidebar mount, which is exactly when the sidebar becomes visible, and reports the pane's datasource — `mixed` for a Mixed pane.
* The three card-level events fire from `MetricsList` and report the card's own query datasource. Expanding a metric and selecting one for its metadata are both toggles, so each reports only its opening half.
* Search is debounced at 300ms and reports the term's length and how many metrics it matched, never the term itself, which can echo back label values from the user's own data. It skips a catalog that has not arrived and will not re-report a term the user did not retype.
* `user_id` from the spec is omitted, since the RudderStack backend already calls `identify()` at init and attaches identity server-side. `stacked_data_source_count` is named `stacked_queries_count`, because the sidebar renders one card per query and two queries can share a datasource.

## Risks


Low. The only behavioural change outside the tracking calls is that `MetricsList` now takes a `stackedQueriesCount` prop and keeps two extra refs, neither of which affects rendering. `data_source_type` deliberately means the pane's datasource on `panel_opened` and the card's query datasource on the other three, so grouping all four by that property in one query will not join up — this is documented on the shared type and pinned by a test.

## Demo


N/A

## Testing Instructions

* Enable `grafana.exploreMetricsSidebar` and open Explore with a Prometheus datasource; the "Datasource explorer" sidebar appears and `signal_explorer_panel_opened` is sent.
* Expand a card, then expand a metric row and click a metric name; `signal_explorer_metric_expanded` and `signal_explorer_metrics_metadata_viewed` are sent, and collapsing or deselecting sends nothing.
* Type into the metric search box; one `signal_explorer_search_performed` is sent after you stop typing, carrying only `search_term_length` and `result_count`. Changing the time range afterwards sends nothing further.
* Turn the flag off and confirm Explore emits none of these events.

Title: Unified storage: decide selector push-down from the manifests, not the build

A LIST with a field selector only went through search when the group appeared in the manifest list compiled into the binary. A kind from an app this binary does not know about was left on the store scan, which pages over the whole collection and filters afterwards, so early pages come back empty with just a continue token.

The decision now reads the kind declarations the index mapping is built from, which the manifest watcher keeps up to date. So an app kind gets its selectors pushed down once its manifest is known, without waiting for a Grafana release.

It is also stricter: every field the request filters on must be declared. Before, any group in the compiled-in list passed, including for a field its kind never declared, and that query reached the index and found nothing.

The registry is now built whether or not the process runs search, because a storage server that delegates search still has to make this decision.

If the declarations are ahead of the index, the search side refuses the filter and the LIST falls back to the store scan (#133102).

Also removes `AppManifestsWithKinds` — no callers left in grafana or grafana-enterprise.

Related: https://github.com/grafana/search-and-storage-team/issues/994 (point 3)

Title: Provisioning: Force-delete a wedged repository from the deletion-error banner ## What Reworks the repository delete UX around the backend's ground-truth deletion status instead of the frontend trying to predict when a delete will wedge. - Deleting a repository is always a plain delete (the dropdown's remove/keep resources options are unchanged). - When a deletion wedges — e.g. the `cleanup` finalizer can't remove a webhook because the repository is no longer reachable — the backend reports it in the structured `status.deletion` field. The repository Overview then shows a **Repository deletion error** banner with a **Delete anyway** button. - **Delete anyway** force-removes *exactly* the finalizer the backend names as blocking (`status.deletion.finalizer`), letting the in-progress deletion finish. A confirm modal warns that provider-side resources (e.g. the webhook) are left in place. The banner also renders `status.fieldErrors` (spec validation errors), which do **not** get the force-delete button — they are not a wedged deletion. ## Why Previously the frontend inspected the `Ready` condition for `AuthenticationFailed` to decide whether to force-delete. Title: Provisioning: Build repository on delete only for the cleanup finalizer

## What
Lets a provisioning repository be deleted even when it is unhealthy (e.g. its credentials have expired), instead of the delete getting permanently stuck — by removing the `cleanup` finalizer.

## Why
In production, repositories got wedged in `Terminating` forever, re-entering the reconcile every resync:

- `error="create repository from configuration: create gitlab client: authentication token has expired: authentication failed"` — deleting builds the repository (decrypt secrets + construct the provider client), which fails on expired credentials.
- `error="process finalizers: execute deletion hooks: delete webhook: permission denied"` — the webhook DELETE the `cleanup` finalizer performs was rejected.

Of the four finalizers, only `cleanup` (webhook removal) needs a working provider client; the others operate on Grafana-side state from the configuration alone.

Ref: grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1374

## How
- **The cleanup finalizer owns the build + webhook deletion, inside `finalizer.process`.** The finalizer is given the repository factory and builds the repository only when the `cleanup` finalizer is present (the one provider-dependent step), then deletes the webhook. The other finalizers run from the configuration alone. `handleDelete` just calls `process`.
- **A build or webhook-delete failure fails the finalizer and blocks deletion** (recorded on status). It is not tolerated — forcing deletion is done by *removing the `cleanup` finalizer*, so the build never happens and expired credentials can't block deletion.
- Dropped the now-redundant `build` deletion-metrics stage; a build failure during the cleanup finalizer is metered under the finalizers stage.

"Force delete" is therefore *removing the `cleanup` finalizer* — a client (the frontend, `kubectl`, Terraform) drops it and deletion proceeds without touching the provider. No new annotation/API surface. Chosen over a DELETE-rejecting admission validator, which would make `terraform destroy` of an expired-credential repo hard-fail with no in-band remedy.

### Error classification (user vs system)
`finalizer.process` only *wraps* a build/webhook failure (`create repository from configuration: %w` / `execute deletion hooks: %w`), preserving the typed sentinel. The controller's delete branch classifies the returned error via `errors.Is`, exactly as it does for health-check failures:

- `ErrUnauthorized` / `ErrPermissionDenied` (expired/revoked credentials) → Ready reason `AuthenticationFailed`, treated as **user-caused**: surfaced on `status.health` and swallowed (returns nil) so it isn't re-logged at ERROR every resync.
- `ErrSecretDecryptFailed` / `ErrServerUnavailable` (transient infra) → `ServiceUnavailable`, treated as **system**: returned to the workqueue for fast retry.
- SLO metrics are labelled user vs system the same way.

This is unchanged by moving the build into `process` — the sentinel still survives the wraps.

## Testing
- `go test ./pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/controller/ ./apps/provisioning/pkg/repository/` — process builds+deletes the webhook only for the cleanup finalizer; build failure and webhook-delete failure each block deletion; process ignores cleanup gracefully when the repo has no webhook client; config-only finalizers run without a build; delete-path classification (auth → AuthenticationFailed, surfaced on health) still holds.
- Integration test in `pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/git/webhook` for the escape hatch: removing the cleanup finalizer lets the repo delete with the webhook DELETE never attempted (requires Docker to run).
- `go vet`, `gofmt`, wider `go build` clean.

## Frontend
The user-facing warning + dropping the cleanup finalizer ships as a separate frontend PR (#133113).

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] No breaking changes

Title: IAM: Implement AuthInfo delete for legacy storage

**What is this feature?**

This PR adds a targeted single row delete for the `user_auth` legacy table.

Implements delete support for the `AuthInfo` resource's legacy-storage REST adapter, which previously always returned 405 Method Not Supported. Adds a single-row delete path (by user + auth module) through `login.Store`, wires it into both the legacy SQL and k8s-client implementations and updates the REST handler to use it instead of rejecting the request.

**Why do we need this feature?**

Any deletion of a single `AuthInfo` object returned 405 whenever the `AuthInfo` resource is under dual-write mode 0–3. Mode 4-5 were unaffected since they bypass `LegacyStore` entirely and go straight to unified storage, which already had a working generic delete. This fix makes auth-method removal actually work end-to-end in the modes that route through legacy storage.

all users

Part of [DPRO-398](https://linear.app/grafana/issue/DPRO-398) and #132935.

The notebook now automatically offers INI and future registered languages. Language metadata has no parser imports; optional language code stays lazy.
